**Attribution**
GeneFíor was developed by Nicholas J. Dimonaco and Katie Lawther. See https://github.com/NickJD/GeneFior for source and documentation.

**What it does**
GeneFíor is a multi-tool gene detection toolkit that searches DNA and protein sequences against reference databases using BLAST, BWA, Bowtie2, DIAMOND, Minimap2, and MMseqs2. It provides transparent, coverage-based validation with evidence qualification and allele resolution.
**Subcommands available as separate Galaxy tools:**
- **GeneFior** — General-purpose detection with user-provided databases - **AMRfior** — AMR-focused detection with pre-packaged CARD, ResFinder, and NCBI databases - **GeneFior-Recompute** — Recalculate detection statistics with different thresholds - **GeneFior-Gene-Stats** — Generate gene-level coverage visualisations and read exports - **GeneFior-Combine** — Combine per-sample detection matrices into combined matrices
**Input types:**
- **Single-FASTA:** A single FASTA file (contigs, reads, or assembled sequences) - **Paired-FASTQ:** Two FASTQ files (R1 and R2) from paired-end sequencing - **Genes-FASTA:** Full-length gene sequences (DNA or protein); skips read-mappers
**Evidence qualification levels:**
- **EXACT_ALLELE_DETECTED** — 100% identity, full-length coverage, allele-resolving support - **CANDIDATE_ALLELE_DETECTED** — ≥98% identity, full-length support, allele-resolving - **ALLELE_LIKE** — strong evidence close to named allele - **FAMILY_DETECTED** — gene family supported but alleles not distinguished - **PARTIAL_OR_DIVERGENT** — incomplete or divergent mapping - **NOT_DETECTED** — insufficient evidence
